resources.string: Real-time aerobic decoupling between power and heart rate (%). Lower is better; under 5% indicates well-coupled aerobic effort. Assumes a steady effort — during intervals or very variable riding the number reflects the intensity change, not cardiac drift.
Heart Rate Variability — RMSSD in milliseconds, calculated from Polar H10 RR intervals via Bluetooth
Live HRV stress, comparing current RMSSD against a rolling 20-minute baseline. 0% = at or above baseline, higher = HRV depressed vs trend. Reads — for the first 5 min while the baseline settles.

Detrended Fluctuation Analysis short-term scaling exponent. ≈1.0 at easy aerobic effort, drops toward 0.5 above threshold. 0.75 is widely used as a non-invasive aerobic-threshold marker (Rogell et al., 2021). Needs ~2 min of RR data before it reads.
Standard deviation of RR intervals (ms) over a sliding 60-beat window. Captures overall HRV including longer-term variability that RMSSD misses.
Percentage of successive RR-interval differences exceeding 50 ms — a classic parasympathetic / vagal-tone marker. Drops sharply with exercise intensity.
Short-term Poincaré-plot standard deviation (ms). Reflects beat-to-beat (parasympathetic) variability. Sliding 60-beat window.
Long-term Poincaré-plot standard deviation (ms). Reflects total HRV including slower fluctuations. Sliding 60-beat window.
Ratio of short- to long-term Poincaré standard deviations — a parasympathetic-vs-sympathetic balance indicator. Lower at higher intensity.
Breaths per minute derived from respiratory sinus arrhythmia in the RR-interval stream. No chest strap or face mask required. Accuracy degrades at very high intensities when RSA collapses.

Count per minute of RR intervals that deviate >20 % from the previous accepted interval — a rough indicator of premature / ectopic beats. NOT a clinical diagnostic. If you see consistently high values at rest, consult a physician.

Aerobic decoupling between speed (pace) and heart rate (%) over the last 30 min. Same Friel method as Pw:Hr Decoupling but for riders without a power meter (or runners). Speed is terrain-confounded — trust it on steady efforts over flat ground, not hilly or variable riding. Reads — for the first 10 min.

Coggan Efficiency Factor — Normalized Power divided by average heart rate over the last 30 min. Higher is more aerobically efficient. Compare across rides at similar, steady intensity — surges and intervals inside the window distort it. Reads — for the first 10 min.

Skiba W′ balance — the joules of anaerobic capacity remaining (your "matches left"). Burns down above critical power, recovers exponentially below. Defaults: CP 250 W, W′ 20 000 J — personalise via a future settings screen.
Skiba W′ balance as a percentage of full anaerobic capacity — a 0–100 % "matches left" fuel gauge. Same model as the W′ balance field, but readable at a glance without knowing your W′ in joules.
Latches the minute mark at which Pw:Hr decoupling first sustained above 5% — the moment your aerobic ceiling broke. Reads — until the pop happens, then a constant value for the rest of the ride.

Live aerobic-threshold power estimate (watts) — the power at which DFA α1 crosses 0.75 (Rogell et al., 2021). Updates as more α1 / power pairs accumulate; reads — until the regression has enough varied data. Persists across rides — the average is shown on the Readiness screen.
No AeT estimate yet — ride with DFA α1 enabled and the strap paired.
NP / AP — how spiky the ride is. 1.00 = perfectly steady, > 1.10 = punchy / crit-style. Useful for separating "endurance ride" from "interval session" post-hoc.
Coggan Intensity Factor — NP divided by your FTP. 0.65 = endurance, 0.85 = sweet-spot, 1.00 = at threshold. Default FTP 270 W — adjust in settings.
Live cumulative Training Stress Score. TSS = hours × IF² × 100. Builds through the ride; 100 = a one-hour all-out FTP effort.
Cumulative mechanical work done, integrated from the power stream. Approximately equal to dietary Calories burned at typical cycling efficiency.
Percentage of ride time spent at <5 W (freewheeling). Most riders coast more than they think.
Coggan quadrant analysis from power + cadence. 1 = aerobic, 2 = grinder (high force, low cadence), 3 = recovery, 4 = spinning. Reports the dominant quadrant over the last 60 s.
Vertical Ascent Meters per hour — the standard climbing-speed metric. Computed over the last 60 s of elevation gain.
Average HR per watt over the last 30 min — the inverse of Efficiency Factor, expressed as bpm/W. Lower is more efficient. Same information as EF but with a more intuitive scale.
Highest 5-second mean power achieved so far in this ride. Sprint capacity indicator.
Highest 1-minute mean power so far in this ride. Anaerobic / VO₂max capacity.
Highest 5-minute mean power so far in this ride. VO₂max region.
Highest 20-minute mean power so far in this ride. Classic FTP-test duration; ≈95 % gives an FTP estimate.
Highest 60-minute mean power so far in this ride — closest single-number proxy for true FTP.
Power-to-weight ratio — 3-second smoothed power divided by your weight (default 75 kg — adjust in Rider Settings). The number climbing performance is measured in.

FTP estimate from the classic 20-minute protocol — 95 % of the best 20-minute power seen so far this ride. Only meaningful after a hard sustained effort: an easy ride reports 95 % of easy riding, not your FTP. (Not the power-duration-model "eFTP" of Xert / intervals.icu.) Reads — until 20 min of power has accumulated. Per-ride finals are persisted; the 42-day best shows on the Readiness screen.
Rolling FTP estimate: %1$d W (best of %2$d rides, 42 days)
No eFTP history yet — finish a ride with at least 20 min of power data.

Take a 2-minute resting reading with your H10 before clipping in. Compared against your rolling 7-day average to suggest whether to go hard or take it easy.\n\nSit still, breathe normally, and don\'t talk.

These values feed Intensity Factor / TSS (FTP), W′ balance and W′ % (CP and W′), and Power W/kg (weight). Defaults are reasonable starting values; tune them once you know your numbers.
Defaults loaded — press Save to apply
FTP must be between %1$d and %2$d W
Critical Power must be between %1$d and %2$d W
W′ must be between %1$d and %2$d J
HR max must be between %1$d and %2$d bpm
Weight must be between %1$.0f and %2$.0f kg

This app adds three data fields to your Karoo:

• Pw:Hr Decoupling — % drift between the first and second half of the last 30 min of riding (Friel method). < 5% means well-coupled aerobic effort. Field reads — for the first 10 min while the window fills.

• HRV (RMSSD) — real-time heart rate variability in ms, read directly from a Polar H10 over Bluetooth. Pair the strap under Sensors first.

• HRV Stress % — live HRV compared against a rolling 20-min baseline. Reads — for the first 5 min while the baseline settles, then higher numbers mean HRV is depressed vs your in-ride trend.

On your Karoo:
1. Edit a ride profile page
2. Add a data field
3. Pick "Pw:Hr Decoupling", "HRV (RMSSD)", or "HRV Stress %" under Extensions
